---
title: "Check available FFB dataset versions"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to the `funga_version()` function of the `fungaR` package. This function retrieves metadata about the dataset versions of the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) checklist currently published on the [FFB IPT data portal](https://ipt.jbrj.gov.br/jbrj/resource?r=lista_especies_flora_brasil), hosted by the Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden.

Because FFB is a living checklist, continuously updated as taxonomists review and add names, every dataset release is versioned. Checking which versions exist — and which one is current — is normally the first step before downloading, parsing, or filtering FFB data, since it lets you pin your analysis to a specific, citable release.

## Function Overview

`funga_version()` takes no arguments: it simply queries the FFB IPT metadata and returns a data frame summarizing every published version.

## Output columns

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `Version` | Version number of the dataset release. |
| `Published_on` | Timestamp of the dataset release. |
| `Records` | Number of records included in the release. |
| `URL` | Direct link to the dataset version on the IPT portal. |
| `Latest` | Logical. `TRUE` for the row corresponding to the most recently published version. |

## List all available versions

```r
library(fungaR)

versions_df <- funga_version()
head(versions_df)
```

## Identify the latest version

```r
latest <- versions_df[versions_df$Latest == TRUE, ]
latest$Version
```

## Additional Tips

- `funga_download()` and `funga_parse()`, and every function built on top of them (`funga_records()`, `funga_search()`, `funga_match()`, `funga_get_children_taxa()`), default to `version = "latest"`. You only need `funga_version()` directly when you want to pin an analysis to a specific, older release for reproducibility.
- Pass a specific version string from the `Version` column (e.g. `funga_download(version = versions_df$Version[1])`) to work with that exact release instead of the current one.
- The `Records` column is a quick way to sanity-check that a download completed correctly: the number of parsed rows should be in the same order of magnitude.
